Shared parity corpus for the ExtendDB WebAssembly build.
An ORDERED sequence of cases run against ONE fresh engine. It is executed
two ways:
* native — tests/parity.rs runs each case through
extenddb_wasm_adapter::Engine built natively, i.e. sqlx + C
SQLite.
* wasm   — parity/run.mjs runs each case through the browser wasm module
(adapter -> engine -> the synchronous SQLite shim -> bundled
SQLite) under Node.
Each run checks only what a case asserts (its error name and its checks);
neither compares the two builds' full responses with each other. Both
runners refuse the whole corpus if a case does not follow the schema
below; the rows of runner-selftest.json hold the two runners to the same
schema, request bytes and judging.
Each case has these members and no others:
name    human label, a non-empty string.
op      the X-Amz-Target operation name, a non-empty string.
body    the request, a JSON object. It is sent as canonical JSON: no
whitespace; object members sorted by the code points of their
names; in strings, '"' and '\' escaped with a backslash, U+0008,
U+0009, U+000A, U+000C and U+000D written as \b, \t, \n, \f and
\r, every other code point below U+0020 as \u00xx in lower-case
hex, and every other code point as itself.
rawBody in place of body: a request string sent as written, for a request
a body cannot express (malformed JSON, JSON that is not an object, or a
number the rule below refuses). A case has exactly one of body and
rawBody.
error   null for success, else the expected DynamoDB error short-name
(the segment of __type after '#', then after '.').
checks  assertions on the parsed response. Each is one of
{path, equals}, {path, contains} (substring of a string member),
{path, present:true}, or {path, absent:true}, where path is a JSON
Pointer. A success case needs a check whose path is not /__type,
and an error case an equals, contains or absent check on
/message. N values are strings in the wire shape.
save    optional: {name: JSON Pointer}; stores the string at each pointer
of the response under name (ASCII letters, digits and _, not
starting with a digit). In a later case's body strings, each
"${name}" is replaced by the stored value (for ARNs, labels and
iterators the engine generates). Every "${" in a body string must
begin such a reference to a value an earlier case saves; a request
that needs a literal "${" goes in rawBody.
onWasm  optional: {error, checks, reason}. The wasm runner judges the case
against this error and these checks in place of the case's own;
reason says why the WebAssembly build answers differently. A case
with onWasm has no save.
Every number in a case is an integer of at most 2^53 - 1 in magnitude,
written without a fraction or exponent, so that both runners read and send
the same value.
Results that DynamoDB does not order (Scan, BatchGetItem) are asserted only
on counts/membership, never on positional value; genuinely ordered results
(Query within a partition or index) are asserted positionally.
